programme: ZBTB7B (ThPOK) sets the CD4-lineage/effector identity of thymocytes and mature CD4 T cells, driving the same target genes (IFNG, TOX, HLA-E) that the STAT2 arm of interferon-stimulated gene induction feeds into; NFIL3 reinforces terminal effector/regulatory output downstream of that commitment (IL10, IL13, CD40LG, CD86, CD3E). Together these three read as one lineage-commitment-to-effector/exhaustion axis rather than three independent hits.
role_in_a: In COVID-19, this axis corresponds to the well-described CD4/CD8 T-cell skew, exhaustion (TOX-high, IFNG-producing) and interferon-signaling response to SARS-CoV-2; STAT2 sits directly in that response, and its deficiency has been reported to worsen viral outcomes.
role_in_b: In thymoma this is the resident developmental programme: ZBTB7B is the canonical determinant of CD4-versus-CD8 lineage choice during intrathymic positive selection, the exact process a thymic epithelial tumor is positioned to disrupt, plausibly underlying the T-cell export defects and paraneoplastic autoimmunity thymomas are known for.
shared_axis: A tumor that corrupts thymocyte lineage commitment at its source (thymoma) and a systemic viral infection that hyperactivates the peripheral effector/interferon arm of the same programme (COVID-19) would be expected to converge on the same IFNG/TOX/HLA-E-centered output, even though they perturb the axis from opposite ends — developmental origin versus peripheral activation.
reasoning: STAT2 is placed strongly in COVID-19 by both Open Targets (0.98 percentile) and PMID 42382660, and NFIL3 is placed in both diseases by Open Targets percentile and one PMID each; but ZBTB7B — the factor doing the most explanatory work for the thymoma side and carrying the highest concordance (40/40) — has no Open Targets association and no on-topic literature in either disease, so its role rests on textbook lineage biology rather than anything retrieved. That mix of one well-evidenced anchor (STAT2) and one biologically load-bearing but evidentially silent anchor (ZBTB7B) is why this lands as supported/moderate rather than established/strong.
support: PMID 42382660 — STAT2 deficiency and heightened viral susceptibility, places STAT2 in COVID-19. PMID 34348612 — reviews COVID-19 immune-associated genes and their pathway linkage to thymoma, the one paper directly bridging both diseases. PMID 38781720 — reviews type I/III interferon deficiency states including STAT2, touches both disease contexts generally. PMID 42461263 — STAT2 mutation causing a type I interferonopathy, offered as the thymoma-side placement though its abstract centers on interferonopathy/TIMS2 rather than thymoma by name. PMID 37062762 — NFIL3 among dysregulated genes in a COVID-19 gene-signature study. PMID 42327792 — NFIL3 and circadian NK-cell modulation, offered as thymoma-side placement but does not mention thymoma directly.
how_to_falsify: In matched peripheral blood from COVID-19 patients and thymic tissue/blood from thymoma patients, test whether ZBTB7B and STAT2 co-occupy (ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN) or co-vary in expression at the shared target loci (IFNG, HLA-E, TOX) across T-cell subsets. If ZBTB7B target occupancy at these genes is unchanged between thymoma patients with and without T-cell export defects (e.g., Good syndrome vs. thymoma without immunodeficiency), or if STAT2 induction in COVID-19 T cells occurs independently of any ZBTB7B-linked lineage signature, the proposed single shared axis does not hold.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (COVID-19) versus thymus (thymoma) — anatomically distinct but developmentally linked by T-cell trafficking, so the shared signal has to be argued through lineage/effector biology rather than shared tissue context. Only 26-40 of 40 patient-group comparisons support the individual factors, and the two most literature-supported factors (STAT2, NFIL3) sit at the lower end (26/40, 38/40) while the strongest signal (ZBTB7B, 40/40) has zero retrieved evidence. Notably, STAT1, IRF5 and NFATC1 — direct interferon/T-cell-activation pathway relatives of STAT2 — were removed as tissue-generic, meaning the interferon axis highlighted here is only the disease-pair-specific residue of a broader, tissue-common interferon signature filtered out elsewhere, not the whole pathway. The single-view exclusions (KLF9, KLF6, ZBTB4) do not touch this axis, so they do not undermine it, but they are a reminder that this account should not be over-read as more consistent than the counts show.
